description: Sequencer built on a counter, mixing eight of the counter's divisions together in whatever proportions the knobs set to make a repeating control voltage

params.text: Picks which way the counter runs, up or down; a cable in the COUNT input takes this switch out of circuit
Sets the largest voltage the mix can reach, 1V to 10V in 1V steps, divided equally across the eight division knobs
Picks how the counter's eight divisions are worked out: B1 a binary ripple counter, B2 a binary counter, D the decimals 2 to 9, P the primes, F the Fibonacci numbers, E the evens and O the odds
Slews the output voltage so it glides between steps rather than jumping
Shapes the glide, linear at one end and logarithmic at the other
How much that division adds to the output voltage, -10 to 10, so it can pull the voltage down as well as push it up; it counts only while that division is active
Picks what the CLOCK and TRIG outputs follow: in the CLOCK position the clock input itself, in the DIV position only the clock pulses on which some division is active. A cable in GATE overrides it
Reverses the order of the eight divisions across the panel, so the longest division moves to the left; a cable in the FLIP input takes this switch out of circuit

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the counter; there is no clock inside, so nothing moves until one is patched here
A rising edge restarts the counter at the first count of the chosen mode
A high gate lets the sequencer run and a low gate pauses it, taking up again at the next clock; with nothing patched the sequencer runs
A voltage sampled at each rising clock edge, used in place of the SCALE switch as the total the division knobs share, each knob at full reaching an eighth of it; it is held within 10V either way
A high gate counts up and a low gate counts down, in place of the COUNT switch
A high gate gives the DIV gate mode and a low gate the CLOCK gate mode, in place of the GATE switch
A high gate reverses the order of the eight divisions, in place of the FLIP switch

outputs.text: Carries the clock while the sequencer runs: the clock input itself under the CLOCK gate mode, or only those pulses on which a division is active under the DIV mode
A 1ms trigger on each clock pulse the gate mode lets through
The eight division knobs summed for the divisions that are active, scaled by the SCALE switch or the S&H voltage, sampled at the clock edge and passed through LAG and SHAPE
The CV output with its sign flipped

notes: the eight lamps above the division knobs light for the divisions that are active on the current count
this module is monophonic: only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read, and every output carries a single channel
menu: Initialize Division Mix Only — puts the eight division knobs back to their default positions and leaves the rest of the module as it is
Randomize Division Mix Only — sets the eight division knobs to random positions and leaves the rest of the module as it is
